rfm_tuples.M_value: Eight code-P open-market purchases by SIX distinct insiders, totaling $1,501,380 since 2025-01-01. Director Stuart B. Parker bought 25,000 shares @ $36.82 on 2025-11-10 ($920,500, +120% to his prior holdings — 20,717 -> 48,152 net) DURING the interim-CEO period after Lacher's Oct 14 departure. On 2025-08-07 (one trading day after the Q2 print + $500M new buyback authorization), a coordinated cluster of FIVE insiders bought open-market: directors Laderman ($148K @ $49.37), Canida ($98K @ $48.96), Gorevic ($98K @ $49.14), EVP Kemper Life Flint ($50K @ $49.90/$50.33), all 2,000-3,000 share sized. On 2025-06-10, directors Paracchini ($31K @ $61.71) and Laderman ($156K @ $62.24) bought. Code-S sales over the same 12-month window: only $17,469 (Director McKinney 504 sh @ $34.66 in Feb 2026 — likely a Rule 10b5-1 trickle). The earlier 2024-08-21 Parker sale of 30,000 sh @ $61.74 ($1.85M) is OUTSIDE the drawdown window and was reversed: Parker REBOUGHT 25,000 sh at $36.82 (40% below his sale price) in Nov 2025. P:S ratio in drawdown window = 86:1.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: STRONG honest-insider tape. Multiple directors and one named EVP put personal cash into open-market purchases AFTER the Q2 print revealed deterioration AND AFTER the Lacher CEO ouster. A 25,000-share Parker buy at $36.82 is an unusually sized director purchase that would only make sense if the director believed intrinsic value is meaningfully above the post-drawdown price. The cluster on 2025-08-07 (5 insiders same day) suggests Board members felt the stock was attractive at $49 post-Q2. The fact that Parker scaled UP into the drawdown (Aug 2024 sold at $62, Nov 2025 bought back 25k at $37) is the cleanest forensic counter-signal to a SHORT thesis. None of the named C-suite (CEO Lacher, current Interim CEO Evans, CFO Camden, CIO Boschelli, EVP Hunton) sold open-market in 12 months; Lacher's only liquidation event was a Sep 10 2025 option exercise where 87% of shares were withheld for taxes — he still held 167K shares at departure.

rfm_tuples.f: Cross-reference Form 4 transaction dates against the 8-K calendar (CEO ouster, $500M buyback auth, ASR, retention awards, earnings prints, reserve development disclosures).
rfm_tuples.M_value: Capital-event calendar: 2025-08-05 Q2 print + $500M new buyback authorization + dividend declared (8-K); 2025-08-13 $150M ASR with GS (8-K); 2025-10-14 CEO Lacher ousted (8-K filed 10-15); 2025-10-22 Chief Claims Officer Sanders departed (8-K 10-24); 2025-11-04 retention awards for CFO Camden ($775K), CIO Boschelli ($675K), EVP Hunton ($775K) (8-K 11-10); 2025-12-16 Lacher separation finalized $5.72M severance. Insider P transactions: Jun 10 + Aug 7 (two days AFTER public Q2 print, NOT within an undisclosed-info window) + Nov 10 (after Q3 print on Nov 5, after Lacher ouster, after retention-award announcement). All P buys are clustered AFTER public bad-news disclosure — i.e., insiders absorbing weakness in the open window, not selling ahead of it. No code-S transactions in any 30-day pre-earnings window. Parker's only sale (Aug 2024) was 12 months before the drawdown peak and predated the CEO ouster by 14 months. CEO Lacher's Sep 10 2025 option exercise was timed 35 days before his Oct 14 termination — but the F-tranche (85,608 sh) was MANDATORY tax withholding, not voluntary selling, and he retained 167,345 shares (worth ~$5M at cutoff) on his way out.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Timing is CLEAN. Buys clustered AFTER bad news, not before. The most natural lying-detector signal — clustered insider SELLING ahead of CEO ouster or ahead of Q1'26 reserve blowup — is absent. Combined with the Mode-A buying tuple, this raises confidence the drawdown is overdone in the market's view but not in insiders' view.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K narrative (filed 2026-02-11): "Adjusted Consolidated Net Operating Income $225.5M" for FY2025 vs $381.5M FY2024, attributed to "evolving loss patterns and higher defense costs associated with attorney-represented bodily injury coverages" in commercial auto.
rfm_tuples.f: Verify whether disclosed loss-cost pressures have abated or worsened by Q1 2026; compute combined ratio change.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (Q1 2026 10-Q MD&A Specialty P&C — combined ratio table + segment NOI)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2026 Specialty P&C combined ratio 106.7% vs 92.7% Q1 2025 — a 14-point deterioration that puts the segment UNDERWRITING AT A LOSS. Underlying combined ratio 106.2% vs 92.2% (current-year non-cat ratio 84.0% vs 70.9%). Specialty P&C Adjusted NOI collapsed to $0.1M vs $97.9M in Q1 2025 (-$97.8M). Earned premiums down $77M YoY in segment due to lower personal-auto volumes AND a $28.0M Florida Statutory Profit Limit Refund. Cause: "higher claim severity and frequency primarily related to bodily injury and property damage coverages in California." Adverse prior-year reserve development $3.6M in Q1'26 vs $0.7M Q1'25. Consolidated Q1'26 net loss $(1.7)M attributable to Kemper vs net income $99.7M (-$101.4M YoY). For FY2025 the comparable adverse PYD was $76.0M (vs $29.8M FY2024). So the loss-cost pressure DISCLOSED in the 10-K as bodily-injury-in-commercial-auto has MIGRATED to CALIFORNIA PERSONAL AUTO and is the new dominant headwind.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 10-K disclosure framed reserve pressure as a Commercial Auto / bodily-injury issue. The Q1 print proves the underwriting deterioration is BROADER than disclosed and now reaches the core Specialty Personal Auto book (89% of premiums) via California severity/frequency. A combined ratio of 106.7% in the company's main segment is an operating event that justifies most of the -52.8% drawdown. The 10-K narrative was not deceptive — it disclosed the loss-cost pressure honestly — but it understated the geographic and product breadth. Underwriting losses are the operational reason for the drawdown; this is correctly punished by the market.

rfm_tuples.R: 8-K 2025-10-15: "Joseph P. Lacher, Jr. will depart from his role as President and Chief Executive Officer of the Company, effective October 14, 2025... C. Thomas Evans, Jr., age 66, was appointed by the Board as interim President and Chief Executive Officer."
rfm_tuples.f: Verify the nature of the departure (without-cause vs for-cause vs retirement); assess whether the Interim CEO is a credible long-term leader; check for retention-award amounts signaling NEO flight risk.
rfm_tuples.M_value: CEO Lacher (10-year tenure since 2015) terminated WITHOUT CAUSE with $5.72M cash severance (2x base + target bonus) plus continued vesting on equity. Interim CEO Evans is the company's General Counsel since 2015 (joined 1992), age 66 — i.e., a placeholder. Board began external search via 'leading global executive search firm.' Three NEOs (CFO Camden, CIO Boschelli, EVP Auto Hunton) received $675K-$775K cash retention RSUs (2-year vest) on 2025-12-01 — signal of perceived NEO flight risk during the leadership void. EVP Sanders (Chief Claims Officer P&C) also exited Oct 22 with $2.025M severance — i.e., the head of the function that drove the reserve blowup departed 1 week after the CEO. As of cutoff 2026-05-25, no permanent CEO has been named (Annual Meeting on 2026-05-06 elected same 9 directors but Evans is still Interim per Q1'26 10-Q signed by him as 'Interim').
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Forced CEO departure following accelerating reserve adverse development is a textbook governance signal — Board lost confidence in 10-year operator who oversaw the deteriorating UW results. ~7 months later there is still no permanent CEO, and the retention-award disclosure proves the Board is paying to prevent further NEO departures. This is a SEVERE flag against the SHORT-thesis honesty grade BUT does NOT contradict the long-bias insider tape; in fact, the insider buying (Parker $920K @ $36.82 on 2025-11-10) was made DURING this leadership vacuum, which suggests at least one director (Parker, former NYC Police Commissioner of Insurance? — actually a former Progressive exec) thinks the franchise is salvageable at sub-$40.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Item 5: "On August 5, 2025, Kemper's Board of Directors approved a new share repurchase authorization, under which the Company can repurchase up to $500.0 million of its common stock." ASR $150M settled Q3/Q4 2025. Quarterly dividend $0.32/share maintained.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify execution price discipline. Mode B — given the Specialty P&C combined ratio is 106.7%, is the buyback + dividend payout sustainable / consistent with maintaining statutory capital and AM Best rating?
rfm_tuples.M_value: $500M new authorization Aug 5, 2025; $150M ASR executed Aug 13-Q4 via Goldman at VWAP ~$50-55 range (delivered 2,279,203 sh initially); aggregate $195.8M used, $304.2M remaining at 3/31/26; NO buybacks in Q1 2026 (zero shares repurchased). Annual dividend $79.6M; share count went from 63.9M (12/31/24) to 58.8M (3/31/26) — ~8% reduction. BUT: holding company on May 4, 2026 voluntarily REDUCED credit facility from $600M to $350M, framed as 'expense reduction' but it removes $250M of standby liquidity right after a Q1 net loss. Total long-term debt $944M (2.4% / 3.8% / 5.875% senior notes). Total shareholders' equity $2,635.1M (12/31/25 $2,669.4M) — only minor decline, capital intact. Goodwill $1,250.7M is unchanged QoQ. Insurance subs all exceed RBC minimums (per 10-K).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The $150M ASR was executed at ~$50-55 vs the cutoff price implied by -52.8% drawdown (~$30s-low-$40s) — i.e., bought at the wrong price. Suspending Q1 buybacks is appropriate given the underwriting loss but signals Board is preserving capital for statutory needs. Reducing the revolver from $600M to $350M is the most concrete cutoff-relevant negative — it removes optionality even as it saves on commitment fees. Maintaining the $0.32/q dividend at ~$80M annual run-rate vs the Q1 net loss is aggressive; if Q2'26 doesn't normalize, dividend may need to be cut. Capital adequacy is NOT a near-term concern (RBC headroom, $944M debt vs $2.6B equity, $1.25B goodwill intact, no covenant trips), but the financial flexibility is narrower than 12 months ago.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Note 5 P&C Reserves: "In 2025, the net adverse prior year development of $76.0 million included $76.5 million of adverse reserve development on prior accident years which was primarily attributable to evolving loss patterns and higher defense costs associated with attorney-represented bodily injury coverages in the Commercial Automobile product line and higher losses on litigated claims."
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify disclosure exists with specificity. Mode B — assess pattern: is reserve adverse development accelerating, isolated, or recurring? Compare 2025 ($76M) to 2024 ($29.8M) to 2023.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K Note 5 reserve development triangle + multi-year MD&A)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Adverse PYD trajectory: 2023 $5.4M favorable in P&C (per 10-K); 2024 $7.0M adverse (P&C segment level $7.2M); 2025 $76.5M adverse (10x increase). Q1'26 $3.6M adverse continues. Disclosure is HIGHLY specific — issuer names the line (commercial auto), the cause (attorney-represented BI litigation, defense costs), the accident-year impact. This is the textbook 'honest disclosure of bad news' that Signal OS detects. The audit committee disclosed this as a critical audit matter (Deloitte clean opinion). However, the magnitude jump and Q1 carry-over indicate the reserve correction may not be complete; the runoff triangle in Note 5 suggests further development is possible if the bodily-injury severity trend continues.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosure quality is HIGH — this is the kind of transparency that protects from a fraud or accounting-restatement scenario. Not a deception flag. But the absolute level of adverse development ($76M, 10x prior year) is a real operating headwind that explains a meaningful portion of the FY25 EPS halving ($2.31 vs $4.95). Honesty grade: PASS; operating grade: MODERATE. Net: MODERATE under the R/f/M schema.

rfm_tuples.R: Mode B (Signal OS Two-Mode discipline): Given (a) issuer paused buyback in Q1 2026 and (b) issuer reduced revolver $250M on May 4, 2026, what should be true of insider personal-cash decisions if management actually believes the stock is cheap?
rfm_tuples.f: Cross-reference Form 4 timing with corporate capital-return decisions to test consistency of management's behavior between corporate cash and personal cash.
rfm_tuples.M_value: If management believed Q1 2026 underwriting weakness was non-permanent and stock was cheap, the Mode-B prediction is: NEO open-market purchases AFTER Q1 print or after the May 4 revolver cut. Actual Q1'26 + post-Q1'26 P transactions (since 2026-02-04 8-K earnings): ZERO open-market purchases by ANY insider. The May 6-7 8-K cluster (Q1 earnings + revolver reduction + annual meeting) was followed by ZERO P buying in the May 8 Form 4 wave (10 Form 4s on May 8 — all of them Code-A director annual equity grants of 4,730 sh @ $32.77, NOT open-market). This is the Mode-B GAP: the insider-purchase tape from June-November 2025 is NOT repeating in 2026 after Q1's underwriting collapse. Even Parker (the $920K Nov 2025 buyer) did NOT add. The implication: insiders thought the stock was attractive at $36-50 in mid-2025 (when the issue was 'reserve correction for commercial auto'), but they have NOT scaled in at the lower current prices when the issue is 'California personal-auto underwriting at 106% combined.' This is a meaningful absence-of-signal.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B catch. The bullish reading would be that insiders' confidence in mid-2025 has not been re-asserted in 2026 after the Q1 reveal. Three possible readings: (1) blackout windows constrain timing (May 8 was just 1 day after Q1 8-K and 2 days after annual meeting — director quiet-period typically extends 24-48 hours post-earnings, then opens); (2) insiders also surprised by Q1 California severity and are re-underwriting their conviction; (3) Parker's Nov 2025 buy was idiosyncratic, not a board-wide signal. The PRESENCE of strong insider buying through 2025 is still a POSITIVE Signal OS finding, but the ABSENCE post-Q1 should temper the LONG-tier conviction.

rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1'26 10-Q Note: Goodwill unchanged at $1,250.7M. 10-K Critical Accounting Estimate disclosure: "Market declines or other events impacting the fair value of a reporting unit could result in a goodwill impairment." Prior goodwill impairment of $45.5M was taken in 2023 on a divested reporting unit. The Specialty P&C reporting unit carries the majority of the $1.25B. With market cap implied at -52.8% drawdown (market cap roughly $1.7-1.9B against $2.6B book), the stock is trading below book value. If management's Step 1 goodwill test uses public market cap as a sanity check, FY2026 goodwill testing (Q4) is a real risk if the underwriting loss persists into Q2 2026. No impairment in Q1 2026 — but Q1 is not the annual testing date.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Goodwill carrying value at $1.25B against a market cap below book is the standard 'next shoe to drop' setup for an insurance writedown. No current GAAP impairment but the Mode-B implied verification is that management has NOT preemptively impaired despite the share-price signal. Disclosure-quality is fine (critical accounting estimate is named); the EXPECTED FY26 annual-test risk is the elevated implied-verification finding. Not severe today, moderate.

summary: KMPR is a -52.8% drawdown specialty-auto insurer where the FORENSIC tape produces a MIXED but tilting-honest verdict. STRONG long-bias signal: 8 open-market code-P purchases by 6 distinct insiders ($1.50M, P:S 86:1 in the drawdown window), including a 25,000-share director Parker buy at $36.82 in Nov 2025 (during interim-CEO vacuum, after he sold at $62 in Aug 2024) and a 5-insider Aug 7 2025 cluster buy after the Q2 print. CEO Lacher's exit was forced (without-cause, $5.72M severance) but he sold ZERO open-market in 12 months and retained 167K shares; no clustered pre-bad-news insider selling. SEVERE operational underdelivery: Q1 2026 Specialty P&C combined ratio jumped to 106.7% from 92.7%, segment Adjusted NOI collapsed from $97.9M to $0.1M, consolidated swung to a $1.7M loss vs $99.7M income. The 10-K's framing of reserve pressure as a commercial-auto/bodily-injury issue understated breadth — Q1 2026 reveals California personal-auto severity is now the dominant headwind. Auditor (Deloitte) clean, no going-concern, ICFR effective, no restatements, no SC 4.02 — honest distress, not accounting fraud. Mode-B gap: no insider buying since Q1 2026 print, despite drawdown deepening — insiders' mid-2025 conviction has NOT been reasserted at lower prices. Capital position adequate (RBC headroom, $2.6B equity, $944M debt) but $250M revolver reduction on May 4 narrows flexibility. Verdict: NEUTRAL with mild LONG tilt. The insider buying through November 2025 is the strongest Signal OS countersignal in this name, but the absence post-Q1 print prevents a full LONG-tier rating; the underwriting deterioration is real and severe; honesty grade is HIGH. Severity: 3 PASS / 4 MODERATE / 2 SEVERE / 0 RED_FLAG / 0 UNVERIFIABLE.
